transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we approach the August 25 production policy review for the public API rate-limit project, I'd like to get the ball rolling. Per our normal review process, I need backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations to report your release-impacting findings before I record the final policy. For context, the current draft allows 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, applies the same limit to authentication endpoints, and doesn't specify a staffed launch window. Please share any findings or concerns you have so I can make a well-informed final decision on what we communicate to customers.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from backend engineering. While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Backend's load replay confirms the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. I hadn't updated the draft because the client test was owned by another team, but this is critical for the policy decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from customer success. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that its contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered the clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this contractual notice requirement needs to factor into the policy decision and customer communication timing.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from security. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. The finding is not yet in the security tracker because the investigation is still being closed, but this directly contradicts the draft policy's current 100 requests per minute limit applied to authentication endpoints and needs to factor into the final policy decision.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from support operations. We confirmed today that the staffed launch team is available only from exactly 10:00 to 12:00 UTC on September 15, with an escalation handoff documented for that window. I haven't added the coverage block to the launch plan yet because scheduling approval finished after the plan was circulated, but this is the only staffed launch window we can support, and it needs to factor into the final policy decision and customer communication.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Update the draft policy to set the ordinary API-key limit to 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window per backend engineering's load replay findings.
Update the draft policy to set a separate authentication endpoint limit of 30 requests per minute per API key, replacing the previous 100 requests per minute same-limit approach.
Send contractual notice to Acme and all affected customers no later than September 1 to satisfy the 14-calendar-day notice requirement, enabling enforcement on September 15.
Add the staffed launch window of 10:00 to 12:00 UTC on September 15 to the launch plan and align the production launch to that window.
